change.title: pr-38446-flat
change.description: Implement recovery key support for user storage providers
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Regenerated codes stored in user storage leave older local codes valid
findings.body: The local branch deletes existing local recovery codes before creating new ones (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:39-40). The user-storage branch (CredentialHelper.java:126-127) does not. UserCredentialManager.isValid runs every local CredentialInputValidator on inputs the storage did not accept (UserCredentialManager.java:59-79), and the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid still accepts codes from the previous set (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:99-112). Scenario: a user has local codes, then a user-storage provider that accepts recovery codes is configured, and the user regenerates. Old local codes keep working and the user is not told. Fix: when the storage accepts the update, remove existing local recovery-code credentials as the local createCredential does. Confidence is medium because it needs a user who already had local codes.
findings.originReason: In the base, the required action always called the local createCredential, which removes the old codes; the new storage branch skips that call.

verification.reason: When storage accepts the update, createRecoveryCodesCredential skips the local createCredential, which is the only place old local codes get deleted (provider lines 39-40). UserCredentialManager.isValid then runs the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider on any input the storage rejected, so a code from the old local set still validates. Before this change every federated user's codes were stored locally, so a user who had codes before the provider gained support will hit this.

findings.title: Exhausted storage-backed codes are removed from the local store only
findings.body: After a successful login the authenticator removes the credential by the id of whatever RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential returned (lines 85-88). That lookup now prefers user-storage credentials (RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:56-61), but removeStoredCredentialById goes to the local or federated store (UserCredentialManager.java:114-117; JpaUserFederatedStorageProvider.java:601-602), so the storage copy is never removed. A storage model without an id would reach em.find(..., null), which throws IllegalArgumentException under the JPA spec, so the login fails. In-tree, the test provider never exhausts codes and its models have no id (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:237-242), so this is not reached today. Question for the author: which id should storage-backed credentials carry, and should exhaustion be handled by the provider?
findings.originReason: The diff changed the lookup from local stored credentials to getCredential, which prefers user-storage credentials.

verification.reason: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential now returns the storage provider's model first, but removeStoredCredentialById only reaches the federated/local JPA store (getStoreForUser), never the storage provider, so a storage copy is never removed. A storage model without an id goes to em.find(..., null). As the finding says, this is unreachable in-tree today.

findings.title: Test provider never consumes a recovery code, so reuse and exhaustion are untested
findings.body: The recovery branch of isValid accepts any matching code on every call (line 340). It never removes the used code, unlike RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid, which removes it and updates the store (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:110-111). testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:241-269) logs in once. Nothing asserts that a second use fails, that a wrong code is rejected, or that exhaustion works, so the exhaustion branch in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:85-92 is untested for storage-backed codes. Either state in the provider that consumption is the provider's job and test it, or add the single-use assertion.
findings.originReason: The recovery-code validation branch was added by this diff.

verification.reason: The test provider's recovery branch in isValid only checks anyMatch and never removes the used code. The test logs in once with a code and never checks that a reused code is rejected, a wrong code fails, or the codes can run out.

findings.title: getCredentials drops the recovery-code id, so the entry cannot be removed by id
findings.body: The OTP entry keeps its id (the OTP path sets one at line 179 and returns the stored model at line 248). The recovery entry is rebuilt with createFromValues (lines 237-241), which sets no id (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:58-76), even though the update path sets one (line 195). The removal path matches federated credentials by id (CredentialDeleteHelper.java:63-64) and otherwise throws NotFound (CredentialDeleteHelper.java:81). Also, the test provider's disableCredentialType and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream handle only OTP (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:216-223, 258-261), so if removal reaches the type-based path (CredentialDeleteHelper.java:68), it reports success and the codes keep working. Fix: copy the stored id onto the returned model. Whether the account REST listing exposes this entry was not verified.
findings.originReason: This diff added the getCredentials override and the recovery-code support in the test provider.

verification.reason: getCredentials rebuilds the recovery entry with createFromValues, which never sets an id, so the id stored at line 195 is lost and CredentialDeleteHelper's id match at line 64 can't find the entry. disableCredentialType and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream only handle OTP, so the type-based fallback leaves the codes in place.

contracts.action: Recovery code setup from the required action writes codes to user storage when the storage accepts them
contracts.before_after: Before: the action called the local provider's createCredential directly, which deletes existing local codes and stores hashed codes (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:36-43). After: createRecoveryCodesCredential tries updateCredential first with the raw codes as JSON, and falls back to the local provider only if the storage declines. The OTP sibling uses the same storage-first pattern, but for OTP the stored value is the secret, not a login factor in cleartext.
contracts.visible_effect: The user sees the same code list either way. The storage provider receives plaintext codes and the local store is not cleared when the storage accepts.
contracts.failure_mode: Codes are stored in cleartext in user storage (see finding 1). Older local codes stay valid when the storage accepts the update (see finding 2).

contracts.action: Recovery code login looks up the recovery credential, preferring user storage, before handling exhaustion
contracts.before_after: Before: getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream, local store only. After: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential checks getFederatedCredentialsStream first, then the local store. The lookup now also calls the storage provider's getCredentials on each login.
contracts.visible_effect: Federated users now reach the exhaustion branch with the storage credential. When every code is used, the required action is added.
contracts.failure_mode: Removal goes to the local or federated store by the storage id, so the storage copy is not removed. A storage model without an id would make the JPA lookup throw (see finding 3).
contracts.open_question: Which id should a user-storage recovery credential carry, and should exhaustion of storage-backed codes be handled by the provider rather than by removeStoredCredentialById?

contracts.action: Recovery code login consumes the matched code
contracts.before_after: Before/local: the validator removes the used code and writes the credential back. Storage: the validator only compares and returns a boolean, with no removal or write-back.
contracts.visible_effect: For storage-backed codes in the test provider, a used code stays valid for later logins.
contracts.failure_mode: A used code is accepted again. This is silent.
contracts.open_question: Is consumption of storage-backed codes the provider's responsibility? The core contract is not documented, and the test provider does not consume.

contracts.action: Login form shows the recovery code number to enter
contracts.before_after: Before: local store only, findFirst().get(). After: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential (storage first), then the same .get(). The empty-case behaviour is unchanged.
contracts.visible_effect: The prompt shows the number of the next code in the credential it found (theme login-recovery-authn-code-input.ftl:10 in theme/base and keycloak.v2).
contracts.failure_mode: If the user has both a storage set and a local set, the prompt can show a number from one set while the other set validates the code. Empty case: Optional.get throws, as before.

contracts.action: Recovery credential lookup calls the storage provider's getCredentials
contracts.before_after: Before: one local store query. After: a storage call (getFederatedCredentialsStream), then the local query only when the storage has none. The storage call runs on the login form render and during authentication.
contracts.visible_effect: Federated users see the stored code set; users with no storage provider see no change.
contracts.failure_mode: getFederatedCredentialsStream has no try/catch (UserCredentialManager.java:130-146), so an exception from a provider's getCredentials propagates into the login page. The test provider returns null-id models (see finding 5).

contracts.action: Account credential listing shows user-storage recovery codes
contracts.before_after: Before: getCredentials did not exist in this provider, so no credentials were listed. After: OTP and recovery codes are listed. The OTP entry keeps its id, and the recovery entry is rebuilt without one.
contracts.visible_effect: The recovery entry appears in the credential list with no id.
contracts.failure_mode: Removal by id cannot match the entry, and the removal path falls through to NotFound (see finding 5).
contracts.open_question: Does the account REST listing (AccountCredentialResource GET) use getFederatedCredentialsStream, and what id does it expose to the client? That path was not read.

summary: Reviewed all 8 files of this part in full. The main defect is that the user-storage branch of createRecoveryCodesCredential passes the raw recovery codes (not the hashes the local path stores) to the storage provider, so a provider that accepts the update keeps login-equivalent secrets in cleartext; this is a blocker. Next: regenerating into user storage does not remove older local codes, so they stay valid (fix). Lower-severity issues are the federated-exhaustion removal path, the test provider never consuming codes, and the recovery entry from getCredentials having no id. The test's expected code index (0) is correct, because the page object subtracts 1 from the displayed number. No docs/adr directory exists in the snapshot, so there was no ADR to check. No code was built or run.

entries.title: Recovery codes are handed to user storage in plaintext
entries.reason: Handing raw secrets to a user-storage CredentialInputUpdater is how the SPI already works: passwords reach updateCredential in plaintext too, and the provider decides how to store them (the same test provider hashes the raw password it gets). Login also sends the raw code to isValid (RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator:72), so the provider has to handle raw input either way. Whether codes end up stored in cleartext is the provider's choice, not something this change forces; only the in-tree test fixture stores them raw.
